note.label: Abya Yala Under Fire

precepts.why:
Kings tells what the northern kingdom did: “they left all the commandments of the Lord their God, and made them molten images, even two calves, and made a grove, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served Baal.” They made false gods; they served Satan, the devil. They caused their sons and daughters to pass through the fire: today we call it abortion, which is murder. They used divination and enchantments, witchcraft, and “sold themselves to do evil in the sight of the Lord”. So the Lord removed them out of his sight.

Our people were always into idolatry, and Hosea says it in one line: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” Joined to idols. Idols, idols, idols. Leave him alone.

And it is still so today. You get it in Santería, brujería, Catholicism; this is what our people, the northern kingdom, the so-called Latinos, are into. That is why the curses keep following us: we want to celebrate witchcraft and idolatry, and the Most High is jacking us up, with earthquakes, puppet presidents and our lands being taken. Why? Because we don't learn. It is all to bring us back to repentance and to the remembrance of who we are.

precepts.text: Heathens from Babylon and Cuthah were planted in Samaria, and each nation made its own gods in the high places the Samaritans had made.
precepts.point: Shalmaneser besieged Samaria for three years and carried Israel to Halah, Habor and the cities of the Medes. The scattered tribes moved further east, into Iran, Russia, China and Japan.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
“In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years”. Ahaz, wicked and weak, was over Judah, and Hoshea was over Ephraim, the northern kingdom. Hoshea “did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him”.

“Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria”. This is Pul’s son. In 1 Chronicles 5 it was Pul, Tiglath-pileser, who came first and took Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh; now his son Shalmaneser comes and does the most. The northern kingdom was not taken all at once. It was done in waves: one group taken out here, some of Reuben, some of Asher there, until almost all of Ephraim was out of the land.

Hoshea became his servant and paid him, then conspired against him: “he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and brought no present to the king of Assyria”. He tried to align himself with Egypt to defy Assyria, so the king of Assyria bound him in prison, “went up to Samaria, and besieged it three years”, and “carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes”. That is modern day Iran, bordering Russia. From there our people kept migrating further and further east: the northern kingdom became Scythians, moving from Iran into Russia, some as far as China, some as far as Japan, where they became samurai.

Why it happened: “the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God”, and they “did secretly those things that were not right”. They thought God wasn’t watching; he saw it all. They built high places in every city, “rejected his statutes, and his covenant”, “followed vanity, and became vain, and went after the heathen”. So “the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only”. Yet “Judah kept not the commandments” either, and “the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel”. God was done with all twelve: the northern kingdom into captivity, and Judah next.

Then the land was filled with heathen: “the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel”. The Lord sent lions to kill them for their evil, so a priest was brought back to teach them “the manner of the God of the land”, how to sacrifice so they could stay in the land in Ephraim’s absence. “Howbeit every nation made gods of their own, and put them in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans had made”. The northern kingdom was called Samaritans because Samaria was their capital, and these heathen sacrificed in the very high places Ephraim made for their idols. And “the men of Babylon made Succoth–benoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima”.

So the carrying away in 1 Chronicles 5:26 was the start of this: God himself stirred up the kings of Assyria against the tribes that went whoring after other gods, and the northern kingdom was broken and scattered, with strangers set in their place.

precepts.text: Israel secretly built high places, set up images and groves under every green tree, and served idols, whereof the Lord had said, ye shall not do this thing.
precepts.point: Because Israel served the gods of the nations, the Most High gave those nations the rule over Israel; that is how they became the oppressor, and the word says envy not the oppressor and choose none of his ways. Unlearned and lost brothers and sisters today are still serving other gods, whatever the religion calls itself.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
Israel was told to utterly destroy all the places where the nations served their gods, “upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under every green tree”. Even after being warned, Israel was still idolatrous. “And the children of Israel did secretly those things that were not right against the Lord their God, and they built them high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city. And they set them up images and groves in every high hill, and under every green tree”.

The very places they were commanded to destroy, they built. “And there they burnt incense in all the high places, as did the heathen whom the Lord carried away before them; and wrought wicked things to provoke the Lord to anger: For they served idols, whereof the Lord had said unto them, Ye shall not do this thing.” The Lord carried the heathen away before Israel for those very works, and Israel did them secretly in every city.

Because Israel served the gods of the nations, the Most High gave those nations the rule over Israel. That is how they became the oppressor. And unlearned and lost brothers and sisters today are still serving other gods, whatever the religion calls itself.

precepts.text: The law had already commanded Israel to destroy such high places, not build them.
precepts.point: They wrought wicked things to provoke the Most High and served idols, though He had said plainly, ye shall not do this thing.

note.label: 2 Kings 17: The Carrying Away of Israel

precepts.why:
“Ye shall utterly destroy all the places, wherein the nations which ye shall possess served their gods, upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under every green tree.” Overthrow their altars, break their pillars, burn their groves, hew down their graven images.

The law had already commanded Israel to destroy such high places, not build them. Instead Israel “built them high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city. And they set them up images and groves in every high hill, and under every green tree.” They walked in the statutes of the heathen and served idols, “whereof the Lord had said unto them, Ye shall not do this thing.” That is why the captivity came.

precepts.text: He that believeth in the Most High taketh heed to the commandments, tying true belief to obedience.
precepts.point: They caused their sons and daughters to pass through the fire, used divinations and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil.

note.label: 2 Kings 17: The Carrying Away of Israel

precepts.why:
“He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment; and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.”

True belief is tied to obedience. Israel hardened their necks “like to the neck of their fathers, that did not believe in the Lord their God”, and the proof they did not believe is that they rejected his statutes and his covenant.

To believe in the Most High is to take heed to the commandments. Those who claim belief while breaking the commandments do not truly believe.

precepts.text: Israel was warned not to corrupt themselves by worshipping the host of heaven.
precepts.point: They caused their sons and daughters to pass through the fire, used divinations and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil.

note.label: 2 Kings 17: The Carrying Away of Israel

precepts.why:
Israel was warned, “Lest ye corrupt yourselves, and make you a graven image”, the likeness of male or female, beast, fowl, creeping thing or fish. “And lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them.”

They did every part of it. They “made them molten images, even two calves, and made a grove, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served Baal.” They corrupted themselves exactly as the law said not to, and the Most High testified against them by all the prophets and seers before he brought the judgment.

precepts.text: The Most High moved Israel to jealousy and anger, foretelling their rejection among the nations.
precepts.point: This rejection is why the seed of Israel are later called heathens and Gentiles in the New Testament, which resolves much of the struggle over Jews and Gentiles there.

note.label: 2 Kings 17: The Carrying Away of Israel

precepts.why:
“They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.”

Israel provoked the Most High with their vanities, and he was very angry and “removed them out of his sight.” He “rejected all the seed of Israel, and afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of spoilers, until he had cast them out of his sight.” This foretells their rejection among the nations.

That rejection is why the seed of Israel are later called heathens and Gentiles in the New Testament, and it resolves much of the struggle over Jews and Gentiles there.

precepts.text: No man can buy or redeem the nation out of its condition, for the curses come from forsaking the Most High.
precepts.point: These settler nations feared the Most High yet served their graven images to this day, and as a nation Israel does the same, serving the gods of the nations.

note.label: 2 Kings 17: The Carrying Away of Israel

precepts.why:
The law says, “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.”

The curses come from forsaking the Most High, so no man can buy or redeem the nation out of its condition. No nation and no treaty can do it. The covenant said, “the Lord your God ye shall fear; and he shall deliver you out of the hand of all your enemies.” Only turning to the Most High can.

“Howbeit they did not hearken, but they did after their former manner.” The settler nations feared the Lord and served their graven images to this day, and as a nation Israel does the same, serving the gods of the nations. So the curses stay on them.

precepts.text: Judah kept not the commandments, so the Most High rejected the seed of Israel and delivered them into the hand of spoilers.
precepts.point: Because their rage and tumult came up to His ears, the Most High will put His hook in Sennacherib's nose and His bridle in his lips, and turn him back the way he came, which joins with the blast promised in verse 7.

note.label: 2 Kings 19: The Most High Defends Jerusalem

precepts.why:
“Also Judah kept not the commandments of the Lord their God, but walked in the statutes of Israel which they made. And the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel, and afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of spoilers.”

That is why Assyria had power to come up at all. The Most High answers Sennacherib, “Hast thou not heard long ago how I have done it, and of ancient times that I have formed it? now have I brought it to pass, that thou shouldest be to lay waste fenced cities into ruinous heaps.” He gave Assyria the very ability to lay the cities waste, for his own purpose, because his people kept not his commandments.

But Assyria boasted with the multitude of his chariots, the same as a nation today boasting of its army, military and political system, and lifted his eyes against the Holy One of Israel. So the spoiler is turned back: “I will put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest.”

precepts.text: The king of Assyria brought men from Babylon and other cities and placed them in Samaria instead of Israel.
precepts.point: These were peoples the king of Assyria had brought into the land, not true worshippers but taught only to appease the God of the land.

note.label: Ezra 4: The Adversaries Halt the Building

precepts.why:
The adversaries who came to Zerubbabel say they have sacrificed to the God of Israel “since the days of Esar–haddon king of Assur, which brought us up hither.” Second Kings tells who they were: “the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel: and they possessed Samaria, and dwelt in the cities thereof.”

So these were not Israel. They were peoples the king of Assyria had brought into the land and set in Samaria in the place of the children of Israel. When they said “we seek your God, as ye do”, they were strangers the Assyrian had planted there, and that is why they were the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin and not brethren building with them.

precepts.text: Not fearing the Lord, they were slain by lions, and they reported they knew not the manner of the God of the land.
precepts.point: These were peoples the king of Assyria had brought into the land, not true worshippers but taught only to appease the God of the land.

note.label: Ezra 4: The Adversaries Halt the Building

precepts.why:
When those nations first dwelt in Samaria “they feared not the Lord: therefore the Lord sent lions among them, which slew some of them.” They sent word to the king of Assyria that “The nations which thou hast removed, and placed in the cities of Samaria, know not the manner of the God of the land: therefore he hath sent lions among them, and, behold, they slay them, because they know not the manner of the God of the land.”

That is the beginning of their sacrificing “unto him since the days of Esar–haddon.” They did not come to the God of Israel as true worshippers; they were being killed by lions and wanted to appease the God of the land. That is the worship the adversaries were offering to bring into the house of the Lord.

precepts.text: A captive priest was sent back to teach them how to fear the Lord, yet every nation still made gods of their own.
precepts.point: These were peoples the king of Assyria had brought into the land, not true worshippers but taught only to appease the God of the land.

note.label: Ezra 4: The Adversaries Halt the Building

precepts.why:
The king of Assyria answered the lions by sending a captive back: “Carry thither one of the priests whom ye brought from thence; and let them go and dwell there, and let him teach them the manner of the God of the land.” So “one of the priests whom they had carried away from Samaria came and dwelt in Beth–el, and taught them how they should fear the Lord.”

They were taught only enough to appease the God of the land, and every nation still made gods of their own. So when they told Zerubbabel and the chief of the fathers, “we do sacrifice unto him since the days of Esar–haddon king of Assur”, that was the whole of it: strangers taught by a captive priest to fear the Lord alongside their own gods. That is why Judah and Benjamin could not let them build the temple unto the Lord God of Israel with them.

precepts.text: Assyria carried Israel away captive because they had sinned against the Most High their God.
precepts.point: They confessed that the fathers provoked the God of heaven, who delivered them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar and carried them to Babylon. This captivity is read in Second Kings, where Assyria took Israel and later Babylon took Judah.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

precepts.why:
The elders confessed to Tatnai that “our fathers had provoked the God of heaven unto wrath”, so he gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, who destroyed the house and carried the people into Babylon. The captivity is read in Second Kings. First Assyria took Israel: “In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.”

And the reason is given: “For so it was, that the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, which had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and had feared other gods.” Israel went into Assyria for sinning against the Most High and fearing other gods; later Babylon took Judah for the same provoking. That is the history behind the elders' answer: they were the servants of the God of heaven and earth, rebuilding the house that a great king of Israel had built, after their fathers had provoked him and been carried away.

precepts.text: In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria and carried Israel away captive into Assyria, when the judgment came to pass.
precepts.point: She became famous among women, for judgment was executed upon her, the way everybody knows when a woman has been run through. Everybody knew the northern kingdom was gone.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
Here is when the judgment came to pass. “In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.”

Samaria is Aholah. Delivered into the hand of the Assyrians upon whom she doted, they took her sons and daughters and slew her with the sword. “and she became famous among women; for they had executed judgment upon her.” The way everybody knows when a woman has been run through, everybody knew the northern kingdom was gone.

precepts.text: The Lord was very angry with Israel and removed them out of his sight, and there was none left but the tribe of Judah only, when the northern kingdom was carried out and heathen were placed in the land.
precepts.point: Samaria shall become desolate, for she hath rebelled against her God; they shall fall by the sword, their infants dashed in pieces, and their women with child ripped up. This was a future prophecy at the time Hosea prophesied, about Assyria coming into the land.

note.label: Hosea 13: In Me Is Thine Help

precepts.why:
“Samaria shall become desolate; for she hath rebelled against her God”. At the time Hosea prophesied this was a future prophecy, about Assyria coming into the land: they would fall by the sword, their infants dashed in pieces, and their women with child ripped up.

2 Kings records it coming to pass. “Therefore the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only.” The northern kingdom was carried out and heathen were placed in the land; Samaria became desolate as Hosea said.

precepts.text: The Most High was very angry with Israel and removed them out of his sight, and Israel was carried away out of their own land to Assyria unto this day.
precepts.point: Isaiah then prophesied that because Ephraim conspired with Syria, Ephraim would be broken within sixty-five years so that it would be "not a people," and Hosea said the same, that Ephraim was joined to idols and would get no more mercy but be utterly taken away and carried into Assyria. Broken and removed from the land, they lost their nationality, culture, and heritage and were assimilated into the nations.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Therefore the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only.”

“For he rent Israel from the house of David; and they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king: and Jeroboam drave Israel from following the Lord, and made them sin a great sin.” The children of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam and departed not from them, “Until the Lord removed Israel out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets. So was Israel carried away out of their own land to Assyria unto this day.”

Hosea said Ephraim would be utterly taken away and carried into Assyria, and here it is. The northern kingdom was removed out of the land and scattered among the nations. Judah, too, “kept not the commandments of the Lord their God, but walked in the statutes of Israel which they made.”

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

precepts.why:
“Jehoiakim was twenty and five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem”. He did evil in God's sight. “Against him came up Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon”. God used Nebuchadnezzar the Babylonian to take down the southern kingdom. “and bound him in fetters, to carry him to Babylon.” Both kingdoms went down because all of us were evil. The northern kingdom had idols; so did the southern kingdom. That's still what you see in black churches today.

The chief priests and people transgressed after the heathen's abominations and polluted the Lord's house. “And the Lord God of their fathers sent to them by his messengers”. God sent prophets to warn the southern kingdom because he had compassion on his people. “But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words”. They mocked the prophets. It's the same when we're in the streets today. In front of 2819 church, they mocked us: the Israelites are always yelling and screaming. There's no difference. We're the most rebellious people.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why:
“Nevertheless they were disobedient”: we as a nation, as a people, were disobedient, “and rebelled against thee, and cast thy law behind their backs”. For example, the law says thou shalt not steal; what do brothers do? Still steal, and we said ‘ah, the hell with that’.

“And slew thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to thee”. It always starts off with hatred first: the spirit of hatred, and then it leads to the spirit of murder. That’s what it means by “slew thy prophets”. “And they wrought great provocations.”

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why:
“Neither have we obeyed the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in his laws, which he set before us by his servants the prophets.” Every man and every woman here and listening online, take it to heart. Don’t ever read the Bible and say this only applies to that brother or that sister. When you hear these scriptures and these lessons, say that goes for me. That will help all of us, because even as the lesson goes, it pertains to the Bishop too.

“Yea, all Israel have transgressed thy law”. It didn’t say some; it says all Israel. That includes me and you, all of us. “Even by departing, that they might not obey thy voice; therefore the curse is poured upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of God, because we have sinned against him.”

That curse poured upon us and the oath written in the law of Moses is what the class goes on to discuss in brief.

That was the Assyrian policy: take you out of your homeland, place you in a different country, and put the people of that country in your homeland. That is how Assyria broke a people. It is like taking the people out of Jamaica and putting black Americans there.

points: These other nations “feared not the Lord: therefore the Lord sent lions among them”. They “know not the manner of the God of the land”, because they were not keeping the commandments.

points: The king of Assyria sent one of the priests to “teach them the manner of the God of the land.” Reading on, they kept the commandments of the Lord and still served their other gods. But the point is they were learning how to keep the commandments: other nations practicing Judaism.
